expected.name: Isami Ueoka
expected.description:
Isami Ueoka, also recorded as Isamu Ueoka, was an Issei storekeeper living in Hanapepe, Kauai. JCCH records April 1942 arrest, Wailua County Jail and Sand Island detention, then mainland transfer August 1942. Listed confinement includes Angel Island August 1942, Lordsburg August 1942-June 1943 and Santa Fe June 1943-October 1945. He returned to Honolulu aboard Yarmouth in November 1945. This was US wartime civilian incarceration; the archive does not establish an individual criminal conviction. Source: https://incarceration.jcchawaii.org/internees/ueoka-isamu-isami

operations.name: Sigfrid Stenberg

expected.charges: Federal prosecution under the Espionage Act of 1917 and/or the Sedition Act of 1918 (mass IWW trial in Chicago).
expected.convicted: Yes — convicted at the mass IWW trial in Chicago
expected.sentence: ADMITTED TO BAIL, APRIL 2, 1919. The Federal Circuit Court of Appeals ordered thirty-eight of the men convicted in the Chicago mass trial released on bail pending its review of the case; the bonds ran from $5,000 to $10,000, with Haywood alone required to provide $15,000. Fifty-five others convicted in the same case did not seek bail. The order is not the release: each man left Leavenworth when his bond was actually furnished, which for those whose dates are recorded here fell between April 28 and September 28, 1919. Reported in the New York Times and across the wire services, April 3, 1919.
